summary.en: The construction decides what the short word contributes.

body.en:
From season 1, episode 2.

*La cause du décès* appears early in episode 2. Here *du* is the contraction *de + le*: it connects the cause with the death being discussed.

In other contexts *du* can introduce an unspecified amount of something. Likewise *des* has more than one grammatical job. A dictionary's shortest gloss cannot tell you which construction a particular occurrence belongs to.

Look at what comes before the word as well as what follows it. A noun or verb that calls for *de* can create a *de* + an article combination. A phrase introducing an amount is doing a different job.

On replay, resist assigning the same English word to every *du*. First identify the relationship in the complete noun phrase. The “cause” example is a useful reminder that an isolated gloss such as “some” would be misleading there.
